Here’s what the tools show and how the pricing breaks down.

1) Licensing and insurance (from provider records)
- Liberty Electric Services (ELEC-023)
  - Certifications: 
    - “Licensed Master Electrician - City of Philadelphia”
    - “Bonded & Insured”
  - Insurance: true

  - Certifications:
    - “Licensed Electrician - City of Philadelphia”
    - “Bonded & Insured”
  - Insurance: true

So both are listed as properly licensed in Philadelphia and bonded/insured.

2) Why the price is in the $575–$640 range

From the quote details and their published rate sheets:

Liberty Electric Services (quote: $640)
- Published pricing:
  - Base service fee: $145
  - Hourly rate: $120/hr
- Your quote breakdown:
  - Service fee: $145
  - Parts: $185
  - Labor: $260
  - Tax: $50
  - Total: $640

$260 in labor at $120/hr implies a bit over 2 hours of billable time once you include:
- Travel and setup
- Running the new cable, mounting the breaker, making terminations
- Testing/safety checks, cleanup, and documentation

Keystone Power Pros (quote: $575)
- Published pricing:
  - Base service fee: $115
  - Hourly rate: $105/hr
- Your quote breakdown:
  - Service fee: $115
  - Parts: $165
  - Labor: $260
  - Tax: $35
  - Total: $575

Here the $260 labor at $105/hr again works out to around 2–2.5 hours of billable time, plus the base fee that covers truck roll, overhead, and admin. Parts cost is not just “some wire”: it also includes the breaker, box/cover if needed, staples, fittings, and markup on materials.

So:
- You’re not being charged an emergency or off-hours premium (both are marked as “routine” and use their standard base fee + hourly rates).
- The totals line up with what they publicly say they charge (base fee + ~2+ hours of labor + materials + tax), which is very typical for licensed, insured electricians in a major city.

If you were seeing, say, $900–$1,200 for this same scope, I’d be more concerned about a premium; at $575–$640, you’re squarely in the normal “licensed contractor in a city” band, not a bargain-basement handyman, but not an obvious ripoff either.

3) How to choose between them

- Keystone Power Pros: lower total ($575), slightly lower hourly rate, slightly shorter labor warranty (6 months on workmanship), one window: 14:00–17:00.
- Liberty Electric: higher total ($640), higher rating and more years in business, 1-year labor warranty, windows: 13:00–16:00 or 16:00–19:00.
